issues.description: The problem specification and the template expect Rideable.messageOnRide() to be a no-argument method returning a String (UML and textual description show messageOnRide():String and example return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (takes an int parameter) and the Pig/Seal implementations also require an int argument and include speed in the returned text. Additionally, the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. This parameter mismatch between the solution and both the problem statement and the template will confuse students about the correct interface signature and expected return format.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and its implementations consistent with the problem statement and template: change messageOnRide to a no-argument method (String messageOnRide()) and update Pig and Seal implementations to return the string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if a speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement and the template (including Main) to document and use messageOnRide(int speed).

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified without parameters in the problem statement UML and the template Main usage (messageOnRide()), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it in Seal and Pig with an int parameter. This signature mismatch (same conceptual method with different signatures) creates a clear mapping/confusion for students: the example/template call r.messageOnRide() is incompatible with the solution interface and implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) revert the solution to the no-argument signature messageOnRide() and update Pig/Seal implementations to return "Riding on [AnimalType] [name]" (removing the speed parameter), or (B) update the problem statement UML and template examples to include the int speed parameter in messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust documentation/examples accordingly so all three artifacts use the same method signature.
